title: Minimal patch pathway: zero-touch onprem upgrades
body:
Goal: define a minimal, auditable patch pathway for private (VPC/on-prem) clusters that allows low-touch upgrades of control plane components (operators, ingress, runtime images) while retaining strong attestation and a safe rollback path. This is explicitly not the full release handbook — it focuses on an automated, constrained flow operators can run for small security/bugfix patches and kube-level upgrades where high-latency human approvals are undesirable.

Context and assumptions:
- Clusters run in customer-controlled networks (airgapped or VPC).
- GitOps (ArgoCD app-of-apps) is the delivery model for most manifests and Helm chart values.
- Images are signed (cosign) and artifacts have provenance metadata emitted by CI.
- Terraform modules manage infra primitives and must expose a lightweight change contract for downstream operators.
- We can run remote probes and preflight tests via a bastion, or via a short-lived agent installed into the cluster.

High-level flow (minimal-touch path):
1) Patch created in main repo: branch patch/<component>/<semver>-<short-desc>. Includes Helm chart bump (chart/Chart.yaml version), values changes only when necessary, and a signed image artifact reference (sha256 digest).
2) CI produces an attestation bundle: cosign signature + SBOM link + build metadata. CI uploads artifacts to the allowed registry (or generates an ADT for airgapped channels). CI produces a signed tag or digest and posts a PR with links to artifacts.
3) Automated checks run (fast): chart lint, values schema, terraform plan for infra-affecting flags, image verification (verify signature), and smoke test in ephemeral sandbox (if available).
4) If checks pass, an automated PR merge policy applies (e.g., auto-merge for low-risk patches). Merge triggers GitOps reconciliation: ArgoCD sync is requested.
5) ArgoCD executes staged rollout using our staged-canary operator (see rollout policy below). The controller monitors the rollout windows and emits signals to our signal-gathering service (pod readiness, latency, error budget, custom health checks).
6) If the policy detects regressions, a rollback is triggered automatically or an operator is paged depending on severity.

Rollout policy (conservative default):
- Step 1 (0-5 minutes): deploy to 1% of replicas/nodes (or a single canary namespace). Run 2-minute smoke checks (pod startup, readiness, simple inference call).
- Step 2 (5-30 minutes): if green, expand to 10%. Run traffic-driven tests (if integrated) and SLO probes.
- Step 3 (30-120 minutes): expand to 100% if signals remain green.
- Timeout thresholds and fail-open behavior must be parameterized per-customer.

Key safety primitives (must exist for zero-touch):
- Artifact attestation: every image has cosign signature and provenance URL.
- Immutable references: Argo apps reference image digests (sha256), not floating tags.
- Terraform change contract: module inputs that can cause infra replacement must be gated behind a manual approval flag (e.g., apply_on_approval = true).
- Read-only dry-run: capability to dry-run helm/terraform changes and publish diffs to the PR.
- Health probes: cluster-level smoke tests and customer-defined canary checks run automatically.
- Audit log: each automated merge and sync includes the CI run id, signer key id, and operator who enabled auto-merge (if enabled).

Terraform module notes (contract suggestions):
- Every module must document: breaking_inputs (list of inputs that may replace resources), safe_defaults, rollback_strategy, and expected_state_keys. These fields should be small strings in module README and machine-parsable via a terraform-docs output.
- Modules should emit a "terraform-plan-hash" as an output for CI to include in artifact metadata. If plan-hash changes for infra-affecting inputs, the CI job should mark the change as "requires-ops-review".
- Use lifecycle create_before_destroy where possible for critical infra and use replacement_protection boolean for resources whose replacement requires human coordination.

Image signing and distribution patterns (airgapped and VPC):
- CI signs images with cosign using a KMS-backed key. Key material is in an HSM/KMS; private key never in CI logs. The cosign public key is stored in cluster as a sealed secret and used by admission controller when verifying pulled images.
- For airgapped installs: CI publishes a signed tarball (OCI layout) and a signed checksum manifest. Operators manually transfer the tarball via approved channels; a verification tool (cosign verify-blob + manifest verification) runs locally before import.
- Recommended cosign commands (examples operators will use locally):
  - Verify image signature: cosign verify --key cosign.pub <registry>/<image>@sha256:<digest>
  - Verify blob manifest: cosign verify-blob --key cosign.pub --signature manifest.sig manifest.json
- Key rotation: maintain a key-rotation window and a dual-signing overlap. New images must be signed by both old and new keys for a period or the admission verifier must accept multiple trusted public keys.

Argo/GitOps considerations and app layout:
- Use app-of-apps: one root app per customer cluster, child apps for control plane components, runtime, and infra-anchors.
- Avoid automatic Helm value templating at deploy time; prefer pre-rendered manifests checked into a separate artifacts repo for traceability.
- Configure Argo health checks to use our custom readiness probes plus a probe that hits a local smoke endpoint. This reduces false positives from brief transient failures.

Preflight and smoke test checklist (CI + ops agent):
- Validate cluster capacity: CPU/GPU/Storage within headroom thresholds.
- Verify CRD compatibility: ensure operator supports new chart version CRD schema.
- Run sample inference (small prompt) against new canary and compare outputs for regressions (fuzzy match allowed, flag large deltas).
- Validate sidecar/ingress configuration (TLS certs present, egress rules intact).
- Run DB migration dry-run where applicable; must be reversible.

Rollback and emergency paths:
- Automatic rollback: if health signals degrade beyond thresholds, ArgoCD triggers a rollback to the previous git commit (we pin a manifest commit hash per app).
- Operator-initiated rollback: run `git revert` on the merge commit in the cluster repo and push — Argo will reconcile to previous state.
- Hotfix branch flow: branch hotfix/<component>/<digest> created from previous release tag, fast CI build + attestation, manual approval, merge and sync.

Runbook snippets (operator actions):
- Investigate failure: kubectl -n redwood rollout status deploy/<name> && kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/<name> --since=15m
- Force rollback via Argo CLI: argocd app rollback <app> <revision> --server <argo-server>
- Verify image signature on node: cosign verify --key /etc/keys/cosign.pub <image>@sha256:<digest>

Open questions / TODOs:
- How strict should fuzzy-output checks be for model runtime patches? (current prototype flags >10% token divergence)
- Define exact plan-hash algorithm for terraform that is stable across CI environments.
- Decide policy for dual-signing during key rotation window for customers with no network egress.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout):
- Ensure cosign public key is present in cluster (sealed secret).
- Ensure required Terraform inputs are present and marked safe.
- Confirm maintenance window (if customer requires).
- Notify customer slack channel and create ephemeral incident if rollout will touch inference traffic.

Summary: this draft targets a small-surface, highly automatable upgrade path for low-risk patches in private deployments that preserves strong artifact attestation and an auditable rollback. It trades off broad manual gating for observability and short, staged canaries. Next steps: validate in two partner clusters (one VPC, one fully airgapped) and iterate on the terraform plan-hash and verification tooling.

Notes to self: convert preflight checklist into a self-contained binary (agent) that operators can run on-prem without access to CI. Add a small shim to the Argo lifecycle to emit more granular rollout events to Sentry/observability.
